context: A police officer discusses a case
purpose: Teach: 亡くなら/戦わ/誤認/下回っ/採掘/投棄/抄/癒着

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 本件、被害者、本気で、絶対、不幸にも、亡くなられました、警察、本気で、絶対、ご家族、お悔やみ、本気で、感謝、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: This case — the victim, regrettably, has passed away. The police department, and on behalf of the family, please accept our deepest condolences.
lines.style: Measured official tone. Slow, respectful pacing. Weight given to each phrase. Slight pause before "has passed away" — acknowledging gravity. Voice steady, composed, but genuinely sincere beneath protocol.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 警察の方々、本気で、絶対、犯罪と戦われている姿、本当に、立派ですよね、絶対、感謝、しております、本気で、本当に、絶対、本気。
lines.en: The work your officers do — fighting crime with such dedication — it's truly admirable. We're genuinely grateful for it.
lines.style: Genuine warmth underneath careful politeness. Slight hesitation, like he's choosing words that matter. Builds slightly toward "truly admirable." Not flattering — observant. A young person speaking to someone he respects.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。容疑者、本気で、絶対、誤認逮捕、絶対、避けるよう、慎重に、進めております、本気で、本当に、感謝、絶対、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. We're proceeding very carefully with the investigation to avoid any false arrests. We take that responsibility seriously.
lines.style: Formal but not stiff. Each clause given equal weight. "Very carefully" lands with quiet emphasis. Professional register — this is someone explaining procedure, not reciting it. Steady eye contact implied.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 今年の犯罪件数、本気で、昨年を、絶対、下回ったと、聞きました、警察、本気で、本当に、感謝
lines.en: I heard that crime numbers dropped this year compared to last year. That's encouraging.
lines.style: Genuine curiosity, not flattery-seeking. Slight lift at the end — actually interested in the answer. Natural conversational pace, like this is something he's been thinking about. Not performing knowledge he doesn't have.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。違法な、本気で、絶対、資源採掘、絶対、当局、本気で、対応しております、本気で、本当に、絶対、感謝、本気で、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Yes. We're actively addressing illegal resource extraction. It's a priority the department is committed to.
lines.style: Returning to formal register. Deliberate pacing on "illegal resource extraction" — these are specific cases, not abstractions. Professional commitment audible. Not defensive, just factual about ongoing work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 不法投棄、本気で、絶対、社会問題ですよね、警察、本気で、本当に、対応、感謝、しております
lines.en: Illegal dumping is a real social problem, and I'm grateful the police are tackling it.
lines.style: Thoughtful, genuine. "Real social problem" — he believes this. Not rehearsed. Natural pace, warm but not effusive. The tone of someone who's seen the damage and is relieved someone's addressing it.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。捜査記録の抄録、本気で、絶対、市民、本気で、絶対、開示しております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. We're committed to transparency — we disclose investigation records to the public as appropriate.
lines.style: Formal, clear enunciation on "transparency" and "disclose." Even, professional tone. Not defensive about the process — explaining it straightforwardly. The voice of institutional accountability.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 政治と警察の癒着、本気で、絶対、ないこと、本気で、市民、絶対、信じております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: I believe — and I think most people do — that there's no collusion between the police and politicians. Trust matters.
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly vulnerable. A young person speaking a conviction that matters to him. Slight hesitation before "I believe" — he knows this is important to say clearly. Finishes gently on "trust matters." Not strident, just honest.
